🇲🇽📊 <u>Truckers' Strike: The Tax-Break Cut Touches Only 170 of 2,580 Companies</u>

As transport groups blocked highways in 19 states on Monday, El Economista laid out what the fight is about: a cap on the toll-booth income-tax deduction. From 2027, only trucking firms with revenue under 250 million pesos (down from 300 million) can claim it, so 2,410 of the 2,580 companies using it keep the benefit. Opened with no limit under Fox in 2002, the break cost 13.9 billion pesos this year and grew more than fivefold in six years; the new cap recovers about 4.5 billion. "It has no effect on the basic food basket or on freight operations in our country," Sheinbaum said.
banner: TOLL TAX BREAK: ONLY 170 FIRMS LOSE IT

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Chihuahua: Maru Campos Spends Nearly Five Times What Congress Approves on Her Image</u>

Chihuahua's PAN governor Maru Campos keeps blowing through her publicity budget. The state Congress approved 175 million pesos for social communication in 2025; by September her government had already spent 837 million. It happens every year: 190 million approved vs 345 million spent in 2022, 199 vs 586 in 2023, 179 vs 704 in 2024. From September 2021 to December 2025, her government spent 2.5 billion pesos on advertising and media, according to state finance figures cited in Congress.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Alito, Ruffo and Fox: The Old Guard Plans a "Grand Opposition Coalition"</u>

PRI leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno met former PAN governors Ernesto Ruffo Appel (Baja California) and Juan Carlos Romero Hicks (Guanajuato), then joined a video call with Vicente Fox, to build "a great opposition coalition, strong and plural, capable of defending the country and restoring democratic balances" ahead of 2027. Ruffo has been under house arrest in Ensenada since September, facing a federal case over fuel smuggling.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Chiapas: Where Christian Zionism Became the Door for Israel</u>

In the Chiapas highlands, a wave of Christian Zionist churches has turned the region into what La Jornada calls an "Israel friendly" zone, backing Israel through three years of genocide in Gaza. Many of these congregations grew out of the mass expulsion of evangelical families from San Juan Chamula in the 1980s. Funded for decades by sister churches in the United States, some denominations have become "the gateway for Israeli expansionism" into Indigenous communities. The paper recalls that the paramilitary groups of the 1990s, behind the 1997 Acteal massacre, were made up of evangelicals. Netanyahu said it plainly in Brazil in 2019: "We have no better friends in the world than the evangelical community."

🇲🇽✊ <u>STARBUCKS MEXICO OPERATOR: WAGE HIKE WON'T HURT MARGINS</u>

Alsea, which runs Starbucks, Domino's, Burger King, Vips and Chili's in Mexico, expects the 2027 minimum-wage increase and the shift to a 40-hour week to lift its Mexican labor costs about 17%: 12 points from wages, 5 from shorter hours, El Economista reports. CEO Christian Gurría told analysts the company started preparing six months ago and expects no margin loss: "We're clearly working on it and we're confident it won't have an impact." The legal workweek drops from 48 to 46 hours in January 2027 and reaches 40 by 2030.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>UN-HABITAT CROWNS CDMX'S UTOPÍAS</u>

Mexico City mayor Clara Brugada received UN-Habitat's Scroll of Honour, the agency's top award for urban innovation, from executive director Anacláudia Rossbach on Sunday, at the opening of UTOPÍA La Soberana in Gustavo A. Madero. It is the biggest one yet: 300 million pesos turning the old Deportivo Hermanos Galeana, 91,377 m², into 80 spaces for care, health, culture and sport. The UN says the model is already inspiring projects in Quito. Brugada calls the Utopías "factories of equality."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM TO LULA: "THE PEOPLE WON"</u>

President Sheinbaum congratulated Lula da Silva on his re-election Sunday night: "Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won. Congratulations, President Lula!" Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro 51.76% to 48.24% in a runoff where a judge ordered the arrest of a Bolsonaro-allied official in Salvador de Bahia for holding back public buses on election day, and the electoral court extended voting by two hours. Latin America's two largest economies remain in progressive hands.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>INE CHIEF TADDEI RESIGNS</u>

Guadalupe Taddei announced Sunday she will hand her resignation as president of Mexico's National Electoral Institute to the Chamber of Deputies on Monday. Two days ago she was vowing not to back down. Since then, the federal auditor (ASF) reported signs of irregular contracts, conflicts of interest, collusion and triangulated funds, and videos surfaced showing her family's closeness to an electoral-materials supplier. Her statement says protecting the institute must come before any personal interest.
